draft.title: Parts of a wave
card: the distance from one peak of a wave to the next peak. It is measured in metres.
the height of a wave from its rest position to a peak. A bigger amplitude means the wave carries more energy.
the number of complete waves that pass a point each second. It is measured in hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz is one wave each second.
For sound, a higher frequency gives a higher pitch. Pitch is how high or low a note sounds.
draft.remember: Wavelength is a distance, amplitude is a height, and frequency is a count each second that sets pitch.

a.q: Which part of a wave is the distance from one peak to the next peak?
a.why: Wavelength is the distance between one peak and the next. Amplitude is tempting, but it is the height of the wave, not a distance along it.
a.clue: Think of measuring along the wave, from peak to peak.

b.q: Sam plucks a guitar string and hears a low note. He then presses the string to shorten it and plucks again. The new note is higher. What has changed about the sound wave?
b.why: A higher pitch means a higher frequency, so more waves pass each second. Amplitude is tempting, but it is the height of the wave and does not set how high or low a note sounds.
b.clue: Pitch is linked to how many waves pass each second.
